feature1.prompt: The makemigrations command currently generates migration files even when the --check flag is provided. This behavior is inconsistent with other commands such as migrate --check and optimizemigration --check, which simply exit without creating any files. Users are forced to combine --check with --dry-run to avoid unintended migration generation. The desired behavior is for makemigrations --check to immediately exit without writing migrations, ensuring consistency within the command suite.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on modifying the core functionality of the makemigrations command. Update the help text and logic so that when the --check flag is used, the command exits before writing any migration files. In particular, adjust the control flow in the handle method to call sys.exit(1) when check_changes is true, and ensure that the conditional that writes files is bypassed in that case.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py. Look into the add_arguments method for the --check option help text and the handle method where migration files are written. Modify the section that currently writes migrations so that, if the check flag is set, sys.exit(1) is invoked before any file output occurs.

feature2.prompt: The current behavior of makemigrations when using the --check flag deviates from what is expected. Unlike other similar commands, makemigrations --check currently generates migration files instead of simply exiting. This inconsistency forces users to add the --dry-run option to avoid creating files, which is not required by migrate --check or optimizemigration --check. The fix should ensure that makemigrations --check immediately exits without writing any migrations, aligning its behavior with the rest of the command suite.

Ensure that the test asserts a SystemExit is raised when --check is used.
